12904-light.title: Light
12904-light.creator: Unknown
12904-light.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Along the wall which faces the porch, women are waiting, like a curtain of shadow, which yields glimpses of their pale and expressionless faces. With nod or word we recognize each other from the mass. Couples are formed by the quick hooking of arms. All along the ghostly avenue one's eyes follow the toilers' scrambling flight.

2918-the-first-and-the-last-a-drama-in-t.title: The First And The Last A Drama In Three Scenes
2918-the-first-and-the-last-a-drama-in-t.creator: John Galsworthy
2918-the-first-and-the-last-a-drama-in-t.description: A book by John Galsworthy. [With vigorous disgust]  By Jove! [In a voice changed by sudden apprehension]  What do you mean by coming here in this state? I told you---- If you weren't my brother----! Come here, where I can we you! What's the matter with you, Larry?

arxiv-1906-11751.title: The Impact of Preprocessing on Arabic-English Statistical and Neural Machine Translation
arxiv-1906-11751.creator: Mai Oudah, Amjad Almahairi, Nizar HabashComputational Approaches to Modeling Language LabNew York University Abu Dhabi, UAE
arxiv-1906-11751.description: Abstract Neural networks have become the state-of-the-art approach for machine translation (MT) in many languages. While linguistically-motivated tokenization techniques were shown to have significant effects on the performance of statistical MT, it remains unclear if those techniques are well suited for neural MT.

arxiv-2007-15934.title: Towards personalized computer simulation of breast cancer treatment
arxiv-2007-15934.creator: Alvaro Köhn-Luque, Xiaoran Lai, Arnoldo Frigessi
arxiv-2007-15934.description: Abstract 1. Introduction Introduction Cancer pathology is unique to a given individual, and developing personalized diagnostic and treatment protocols are a primary concern. Mathematical modeling and simulation is a promising approach to personalized cancer medicine. Yet, the complexity, heterogeneity and multiscale nature of cancer present severe challenges.

arxiv-2201-01346.title: Exploratory Analysis of Academic Collaborations between French and US
arxiv-2201-01346.creator: George Panagopoulos, Michalis Vazirgiannis
arxiv-2201-01346.description: Abstract 1 Introduction International academic collaborations cultivate diversity in the research landscape and facilitate multiperspective methods, as the scope of each country’s science depends on its needs, history, wealth etc. Moreover the quality of science differ significantly amongst nations [ 5 ] , which renders international collaborations a potential source to understand the dynamics between countries and their advancements.

arxiv-2205-05535.title: Clinical Prompt Learning with Frozen Language Models
arxiv-2205-05535.creator: Niall Taylor, Yi Zhang, Dan W Joyce, Alejo Nevado-Holgado, Andrey Kormilitzin
arxiv-2205-05535.description: Abstract Prompt learning is a new paradigm in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) field which has shown impressive performance on a number of natural language tasks with common benchmarking text datasets in full, few-shot, and zero-shot train-evaluation setups. Recently, it has even been observed that large but frozen pre-trained language models (PLMs) with prompt learning outperform smaller but fine-tuned models.

arxiv-2205-08288.title: Measuring Alignment Bias in Neural Seq2Seq Semantic Parsers
arxiv-2205-08288.creator: Davide Locatelli, Ariadna Quattoni
arxiv-2205-08288.description: Abstract Prior to deep learning the semantic parsing community has been interested in understanding and modeling the range of possible word alignments between natural language sentences and their corresponding meaning representations. Sequence-to-sequence models changed the research landscape suggesting that we no longer need to worry about alignments since they can be learned automatically by means of an attention mechanism.

arxiv-2301-09743.title: The Distribution of Metallicities in the Local Galactic Interstellar Medium Based in part on observations made with the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope, obtained from the MAST data archive at the Space Telescope Science Institute. STScI is operated by the Association of Universities for Research in
arxiv-2301-09743.creator: Adam M. Ritchey, Edward B. Jenkins, J. Michael Shull, Blair D. Savage, S. R. Federman, David L. Lambert
arxiv-2301-09743.description: Abstract In this investigation, we present an analysis of the metallicity distribution that pertains to neutral gas in the local Galactic interstellar medium (ISM). We derive relative ISM metallicities for a sample of 84 sight lines probing diffuse atomic and molecular gas within 4 kpc of the Sun.

arxiv-2306-15161.title: Wespeaker baselines for VoxSRC2023
arxiv-2306-15161.creator: Shuai Wang, Chengdong Liang, Xu Xiang, Bing Han, Zhengyang Chen, Hongji Wang, Wen Ding
arxiv-2306-15161.description: Abstract This report showcases the results achieved using the wespeaker toolkit for the VoxSRC2023 Challenge. Our aim is to provide participants, especially those with limited experience, with clear and straightforward guidelines to develop their initial systems. Via well-structured recipes and strong results, we hope to offer an accessible and good enough start point for all interested individuals.

arxiv-2502-12874.title: Testing for Causal Fairness
arxiv-2502-12874.creator: Jiarun Fu, Lizhong Ding, Pengqi Li, Qiuning Wei, Yurong Cheng, Xu Chen
arxiv-2502-12874.description: Abstract Causality is widely used in fairness analysis to prevent discrimination on sensitive attributes, such as genders in career recruitment and races in crime prediction. However, the current data-based Potential Outcomes Framework (POF) often leads to untrustworthy fairness analysis results when handling high-dimensional data.

arxiv-2505-16518.title: CUB: Benchmarking Context Utilisation Techniques for Language Models
arxiv-2505-16518.creator: Lovisa Hagström Youna Kim Haeun Yu, Sang-goo Lee Richard Johansson Hyunsoo Cho Isabelle Augenstein
arxiv-2505-16518.description: Abstract Incorporating external knowledge is crucial for knowledge-intensive tasks, such as question answering and fact checking. However, language models (LMs) may ignore relevant information that contradicts outdated parametric memory or be distracted by irrelevant contexts. While many context utilisation manipulation techniques (CMTs) have recently been proposed to alleviate these issues, few have seen systematic comparison.

arxiv-2505-20032.title: ViTaPEs : Visuotactile Position Encodings for Cross-Modal Alignment in Multimodal Transformers
arxiv-2505-20032.creator: Fotios Lygerakis, Ozan Özdenizci, Elmar Rückert
arxiv-2505-20032.description: Abstract Tactile sensing provides local essential information that is complementary to visual perception, such as texture, compliance, and force. Despite recent advances in visuotactile representation learning, challenges remain in fusing these modalities and generalizing across tasks and environments without heavy reliance on pre-trained vision-language models.

plos-pone-0009561.creator: Josef Krieglstein, Tobias Kewitz, Uwe Kirchhefer et al.
plos-pone-0009561.description: PLOS ONE research article. Mono-unsaturated fatty acids (MUFAs) like oleic acid have been shown to cause apoptosis of cultured endothelial cells by activating protein phosphatase type 2C α and β (PP2C). The question arises whether damage of endothelial or other cells could be observed in intact animals fed

pmc-11464820.title: Leveraging Open‐Source Geographic Databases to Enhance the Representation of Landscape Heterogeneity in Ecological Models
pmc-11464820.creator: Tiziana A Gelmi‐Candusso, Peter Rodriguez, Mason Fidino, Kim Rivera, Elizabeth W Lehrer, Seth Magle, Marie‐Josée Fortin
pmc-11464820.description: Wildlife abundance and movement are strongly impacted by landscape heterogeneity, especially in cities which are among the world's most heterogeneous landscapes. Nonetheless, current global land cover maps, which are used as a basis for large‐scale spatial ecological modeling, represent urban areas as a single, homogeneous, class.

pmc-11473150.title: Cannabis use disorder: from neurobiology to treatment
pmc-11473150.creator: Bernard Le Foll, Victor M. Tang, Sergio Rueda, Leanne V. Trick, Isabelle Boileau
pmc-11473150.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cannabis has been legalized for medical and recreational purposes in multiple countries. A large number of people are using cannabis and some will develop cannabis use disorder (CUD). There is a growing recognition that CUD requires specific interventions. This Review will cover this topic from a variety of perspectives, with a particular emphasis on neurobiological findings and innovative treatment approaches that are being pursued.

pmc-11475264.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the LabTurbo QuadAIO Common Flu Assay for Detecting Influenza A Virus, Influenza B Virus, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2
pmc-11475264.creator: Chi-Sheng Tai, Ming-Jr Jian, Tai-Han Lin, Hsing-Yi Chung, Chih-Kai Chang, Cherng-Lih Perng, Po-Shiuan Hsieh, Hung-Sheng Shang
pmc-11475264.description: Background: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has highlighted the urgent need for rapid and accurate diagnostic tools for upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs). Nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) have transformed URTI diagnostics by enabling the rapid detection of multiple pathogens simultaneously, thereby improving patient management and infection control.

pmc-11490104.title: Fecal glycoprotein 2 is a marker of gut microbiota dysbiosis and systemic inflammation
pmc-11490104.creator: Fabian Frost, Stefan Weiss, Johannes Hertel, Malte Rühlemann, Corinna Bang, Andre Franke, Matthias Nauck, Marcus Dörr, Henry Völzke, Dirk Roggenbuck, Peter Schierack, Uwe Völker, Georg Homuth, Ali A Aghdassi, Matthias Sendler, Markus M Lerch, Frank U Weiss
pmc-11490104.description: BackgroundAntimicrobial autoantigenic glycoprotein 2 (GP2) is an important component of the innate immune system which originates from the exocrine pancreas as well as from the small intestines. The relationship of GP2 with the intestinal microbiome as well as the systemic implications of increased fecal GP2 levels are, however, still unclear.

pmc-11671213.title: Explainable machine learning model for pre‐frailty risk assessment in community‐dwelling older adults
pmc-11671213.creator: Chenlin Du, Zeyu Zhang, Baoqin Liu, Zijian Cao, Nan Jiang, Zongjiu Zhang
pmc-11671213.description: BackgroundFrailty in older adults is linked to increased risks and lower quality of life. Pre‐frailty, a condition preceding frailty, is intervenable, but its determinants and assessment are challenging. This study aims to develop and validate an explainable machine learning model for pre‐frailty risk assessment among community‐dwelling older adults.

pmc-11689179.title: BUILDING INCLUSIVE COMMUNITIES FOR PEOPLE WITH DEMENTIA: TAKING THE LEAD FROM LIVED EXPERIENCE
pmc-11689179.creator: Alison Phinney, Lynn Jackson, Ania Landy, Mariko Sakamoto
pmc-11689179.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Social citizenship is increasingly adopted in academic circles as a theoretical perspective foregrounding the rights of people with dementia to full participation in their community. However, what this means in practice is poorly understood. Using methods of participatory action research and developmental evaluation, our team conducted a four-year study to learn what social citizenship means from the perspective of people with lived experience, and to put that understanding into action through community programs and services.

pmc-12394898.title: A new generation of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) gold–selenolato complexes as potent anticancer agents: distinct synthetic routes and evaluation in 2D and 3D cancer models
pmc-12394898.creator: Pierre Arnaut, Nestor Bracho Pozsoni, Denys Bondar, Petra Lippmann, Susanne Boschuk, Ivan Semenyuta, Subhrajyoti Bhandary, Kristof Van Hecke, Yevgen Karpichev, Enrico Cavarzerani, Vincenzo Canzonieri, Flavio Rizzolio, Thomas Scattolin, Georgios C. Vougioukalakis, Ingo Ott, Nikolaos V. Tzouras, Steve
pmc-12394898.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Two distinct synthetic pathways are disclosed that lead to new gold–selenolato complexes, stabilized by N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs). The weak base route can provide facile access to phenylselenolate complexes of gold, using both NHC and phopshine ligands. In addition, the pathway based on the carbometallation of elemental selenium enables the construction of a more diverse library of products, based on substituted aryl-selenide fragments whose selenol congeners are not commercially available.

pmc-13041492.title: What is the role of food consumption in the relationships between sleep duration, sleep quality, and cognitive function? A study among Chinese older adults
pmc-13041492.creator: Hao Wu, Xiaona He, Yu Cao, Huiting Chen, Wei Gao
pmc-13041492.description: BackgroundAs people age, declines in physiological functions can lead to changes in sleep and dietary patterns, potentially influencing cognitive function. However, longitudinal evidence examining how food consumption mediates the relationship between sleep parameters and cognitive function in Chinese older adults remains limited.

pmc-13122690.title: Metachronous metastasis of renal cell carcinoma to the contralateral ureter 8 years after nephrectomy presenting as hydronephrosis
pmc-13122690.creator: Kolos K. Nagy, Caroline J. Cushman, Jason R. Jesudass, Seshadri D. Thirumala, Brian E. Nicholson, Donald P. Quick
pmc-13122690.description: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is characterized by a potential for unpredictable metastatic pattern and a capacity for delayed recurrence years after apparently curative surgical resection. Metastatic spread most commonly involves the lungs, bone, and lymph nodes, and involvement of the contralateral ureter is exceptionally rare, particularly when occurring as a true metachronous lesion years after primary tumor resection.

pmc-13448002.title: Diagnostic challenge of human herpesvirus 8-associated multicentric Castleman disease in a patient living with HIV disease
pmc-13448002.creator: Sasiwan Atithammarak, Gompol Suwanpimolkul
pmc-13448002.description: SummaryA man in his early 30s presented with a 4-month history of low-grade fever and chronic dry cough. Three months before admission, he developed persistent low-grade fever, rash and bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. He was diagnosed with HIV infection and started on tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir. Two weeks before admission, he developed right-sided pleuritic chest pain.

pmc-13556877.title: 500. Restoring excitatory/inhibitory balance in OCD; the mGluR2 receptor approach
pmc-13556877.creator: T Robbins, S Gould, A Milton, A Roberts
pmc-13556877.description: BackgroundConverging evidence shows overactivity in cortical regions such as the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), including evidence of increased BOLD activity in cortical structures such as the ACC, orbitofrontal cortex and supplementary motor area (SMA), enhanced error-related negativity, and therapeutic effects of cingulotomy in patients with severe symptoms.

pmc-13585802.title: Multimodal large language models for bladder tumor detection in cystoscopy: a retrospective benchmarking study
pmc-13585802.creator: Yonatan Prat, Husny Mahmud, Abraham Tsur, Menachem Laufer, Dina Orkin, Zohar A. Dotan, Barak Rosenzweig
pmc-13585802.description: PurposeCystoscopic assessment is central to bladder cancer diagnosis, yet visual interpretation remains variable. Existing artificial intelligence approaches often depend on data-intensive models that are often difficult to deploy in routine practice. We evaluated whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs), including smaller and more efficient architectures, can accurately classify cystoscopy images, and whether prompt engineering improves performance.
